questions.q: What are the three levels a filter in the Filters pane can apply at?
options: Visual-level, page-level, and report-level
Table-level, column-level, and row-level
Desktop-level, service-level, and mobile-level
Bronze, silver, and gold
questions.explain: A filter can affect just one visual, every visual on the current page, or every visual across the entire report, depending on where you drop it in the Filters pane.

questions.q: How can a viewer see what's filtering a specific visual, without opening the Filters pane?
options: Hover over the visual and select the filter icon to see a read-only list of filters and slicers affecting it
They can't — the Filters pane must be open to see anything
Right-click the report background
Filters are never visible to viewers under any circumstance
questions.explain: Every visual has a hoverable filter icon showing exactly what's currently filtering it, independent of whether the Filters pane itself is shown.

questions.q: What's the difference between locking and hiding a filter card?
options: Locking lets viewers see but not change a filter; hiding prevents them from seeing it at all
Locking removes the filter entirely; hiding just changes its color
They are the same setting with two names
Hiding only works on report-level filters, locking only on visual-level filters
questions.explain: Lock keeps the filter visible but read-only. Hide removes it from view entirely — typically used for data-cleanup filters a viewer has no reason to know about.

questions.q: What does turning on the Apply button (under Query reduction options) change?
options: Viewers can make several filter changes before the report re-queries, instead of re-querying on every single change
It removes the Filters pane from the report entirely
It automatically locks every filter in the report
It converts all filters to slicers
questions.explain: Without the Apply button, each filter change triggers an immediate query — the Apply button batches multiple changes into one query, improving performance on larger reports.

questions.q: What can you format about the Filters pane to match your report's design?
options: Background color, border, transparency, and separate colors for Applied vs. Available filter cards
Only the pane's width
Filters pane formatting cannot be changed at all
Only the font size of filter titles
questions.explain: Selecting the report background and opening Format gives access to the Filters pane's colors and borders, including distinct styling for applied versus available cards.
